events.title: First proposal of silicon-based life
events.summary: Credited as first to suggest life could be based on silicon rather than carbon. Secondary attribution only; no primary text located.
events.source: Petkowski, Bains & Seager 2020, doi:10.3390/life10060084 (citing Darling & Schulze-Makuch 2016) [PEER, secondary for Scheiner]

events.title: British Association address (UNVERIFIED)
events.summary: Reynolds was a chemist who made over 16 silicon derivatives; the address itself was not found. Do not cite until checked.
events.source: UNVERIFIED; Wikipedia James Emerson Reynolds for biography only [POP]

events.title: Another Basis for Life (essay)
events.summary: Essay listed in Wells bibliography (1894). Text and the widely-quoted 'silicon-aluminium ... gaseous sulphur' wording NOT retrieved or verified.
events.source: Wikipedia H. G. Wells bibliography [POP]; quote UNVERIFIED

events.title: A Martian Odyssey
events.summary: Wonder Stories, July 1934. A pyramid-building creature is realised to be silicon-based; it removes silica bricks from its mouth every ten minutes; the bricks are its waste. Landmark for alien logic (Tweel).

events.title: The Talking Stone (siliconies)
events.summary: F&SF Oct 1955. Siliconies: silicon-based creatures about 2 in long on asteroids that absorb gamma rays from radioactive ore. Petkowski et al. say the Horta is possibly based on them.

events.title: Not as We Know It (essay, Sept 1961 - not 1962)
events.summary: F&SF essay on alternative biochemistry, reprinted in View from a Height (1963). The 'six biochemistries' claim is unverified.
events.source: Wikipedia 'View from a Height' essay list [POP]; contents UNVERIFIED

events.title: Island of Terror
events.summary: British horror film featuring a silicon-based life form with corrosive properties.

events.title: The Devil in the Dark (the Horta)
events.who: Gene L. Coon (writer), Joseph Pevney (dir.), Janos Prohaska (Horta)
events.summary: Star Trek TOS S1E25, aired 9 Mar 1967. Silicon-based rock-burrowing mother protecting her eggs; Spock modifies phasers for silicon; McCoy heals it with silicon cement ('I'm a doctor, not a bricklayer'). Monster turns out to be a mother; miners and Horta collaborate.

events.title: 'Carbon chauvinist'
events.summary: Sagan famously called himself a 'carbon chauvinist' (Rolling Stone, June 1973, as cited).
events.source: Petkowski 2020 ref 9 (Ferris, Rolling Stone, Jun 1973) [PEER citing POP]

events.title: Genetic Takeover and the Mineral Origins of Life (follow-up: Seven Clues, 1985)
events.summary: Hypothesis that silicate clay crystals were the first replicators and carbon biochemistry formed around them. 1982 from memory; Wikipedia cites the 1987 paperback.

events.title: The Limits of Organic Life in Planetary Systems ('Weird Life' report)
events.summary: NRC report published 26 Jun 2007. Only title/date/publisher checked.

events.title: Arsenic life claim (GFAJ-1)
events.summary: Science, announced Dec 2010. Refuted in 2012. Retracted by Science 24 Jul 2025. Cautionary tale for alien-chemistry claims.

events.title: Directed evolution of cytochrome c for carbon-silicon bond formation: Bringing silicon to life
events.who: S. B. J. Kan, R. D. Lewis, K. Chen, F. H. Arnold
events.summary: Science, 25 Nov 2016. An evolved enzyme forms Si-C bonds, which are unknown in biology. Arnold won the 2018 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (directed evolution; from my knowledge, not re-checked).

events.title: On the Potential of Silicon as a Building Block for Life
events.summary: Life 10(6):84, 10 Jun 2020. First systematic review. In no environment is life primarily based on silicon chemistry plausible; sulfuric acid supports more organosilicon chemistry than water; silicon likely only a rare heteroatom in water.

events.title: Phosphine gas in the cloud decks of Venus
events.summary: Nature Astronomy, 14 Sep 2020. Detection widely disputed afterwards (dispute from my knowledge, not re-checked).

events.title: Confronting risks of mirror life
events.summary: Science, 20 Dec 2024 issue (press 12 Dec). Warns mirror-image bacteria could cause unprecedented and irreversible harm.

events.title: Dragonfly rotorcraft to Titan (NET)
events.summary: Launch NET July 2028, arrival late 2034, per NASA page last updated 29 Oct 2026. Titan has liquid hydrocarbon lakes.

relatable_facts.fact: Carbon share of human body mass
Silicon share of human body mass (about 1 g in 70 kg)
Cosmic abundance: carbon about ten times silicon
Diatoms contribute around 20% of global primary production (older estimates 20-50% of oxygen)
relatable_facts.source: Malviya et al. 2016 doi:10.1073/pnas.1509523113 [PEER]; Wikipedia 'Diatom' for older range

relatable_facts.fact: Earth life uses silicon only as silicic acid/silica; no known other silicon chemistry in life
Sponges, diatoms, horsetail and rice all deposit biogenic silica
Disilane ignites spontaneously in air at 0 C; ethane survives oxygen at 200 C
Venus temperate cloud layer 48-60 km, under 100 C, under 2 bar, liquid sulfuric acid droplets
Silicon chips are refined from silica sand
